statement: Canonical-witness consequence of universal witness correctness. Let X be a finite set, let A be an oracle, let C_T={C : tt(C^A)=T} be nonempty, and let D:X×C_T→{0,1} satisfy D(x,C)=L(x) for every x∈X and every C∈C_T. For any selected representative C_T^*∈C_T, D(x,C_T^*)=L(x) for all x∈X. Moreover, for every x, the value D(x,C) is constant as C ranges over C_T. Proof: fix x. For any C,C'∈C_T, the assumed correctness gives D(x,C)=L(x)=D(x,C'); selecting C=C_T^* gives the first assertion. Thus universal quantification over witnesses is equivalent, at the level of correctness alone, to correctness for one representative per nonempty truth-table class. This does not bound the cost of finding or evaluating C_T^*, and does not remove x as a decoder input.

statement: Selector-composition lemma. Let X be a finite input set, R:X→Y a reduction map, L:X→{0,1} a labeling, and C_T a nonempty witness set for each relevant T∈Y. Suppose a deterministic selector S(T) outputs some C_T∈C_T, and a deterministic decoder D(x,C) outputs L(x) for every x and every C∈C_{R(x)}. Then A(x)=D(x,S(R(x))) decides L on X. If R, S, and D have running times r, q, and t, respectively, then A runs in time at most r+q+t, plus the time to pass their outputs between procedures. Proof: for any x, put T=R(x). By the selector hypothesis S(T)∈C_T=C_{R(x)}. The universal decoder hypothesis therefore gives D(x,S(R(x)))=L(x). This holds for every x, so A is correct. Scope: this is a conditional composition lemma; it does not establish an efficient selector for the QE* witness sets.
proof: Fix x∈X and let T=R(x). The selector returns C=S(T)∈C_T. Since T=R(x), this is an admissible witness in C_{R(x)}. By the assumed decoder correctness, D(x,C)=L(x). Thus A(x)=L(x) for every x. The stated running-time bound follows by sequentially running R, S, and D and accounting for output handoff.
scope: Finite-domain implication for deterministic procedures with the stated correctness and selector assumptions. No selector construction, QE* reduction, or P≠NP consequence is proved.

Finiteness and the assumed existence of an accepting encoding imply termination and correctness. statement: Prefix-extension self-reduction. Let Y be finite, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Define E(y,p)=1 iff p extends to a string z with W(y,z). If each E query costs at most q, then for any y with a W-witness, a deterministic selector finds one in at most b queries and O(bq+b) time. Proof: maintain that the current prefix p has a W-witness extension, initially true. Query E(y,p0); append 0 if true, and otherwise append 1. In the latter case a witness extends p by the invariant, and none extends p0, so one extends p1. Thus the invariant persists. After b steps, p is a full-length string and E(y,p)=1 implies W(y,p). This shrinks the exhaustive selector gap to the cost of extension queries; it does not bound that cost for QE* witness sets.

lemma: Fiber criterion for reduction-only decoders. Let X,Y be finite, R:X→Y, L:X→{0,1}, and for each relevant y let C_y be nonempty. There exists D:Y×C→{0,1} such that D(R(x),c)=L(x) for every x and every c∈C_{R(x)} iff L is constant on every fiber R^{-1}(y). Necessity: if R(x)=R(x')=y, choose any c∈C_y; then L(x)=D(y,c)=L(x'). Sufficiency: for each y with nonempty fiber, set D(y,c) to the common value of L on that fiber; define D arbitrarily on other y. This characterizes the reduction-only interface; it does not show QE* has that interface or an efficient selector.
proved_step: statement: Fiber criterion for reduction-only decoders. Let X,Y be finite, R:X→Y, L:X→{0,1}, and let C_y be nonempty for each y in R(X). There exists a decoder D:Y×C→{0,1} satisfying D(R(x),c)=L(x) for all x∈X and c∈C_{R(x)} if and only if L is constant on every fiber R^{-1}(y). Necessity: if R(x)=R(x')=y, choose c∈C_y; then L(x)=D(y,c)=L(x'). Sufficiency: for each y∈R(X), define D(y,c) to be the common value of L on R^{-1}(y), independent of c; define D arbitrarily outside R(X). Thus the condition is both necessary and sufficient. It isolates the interface needed for a fiber argument, but does not establish that QE* uses it or that a witness selector is efficient.

proved_step: statement: Adaptive-cost prefix selector. Let Y be finite, b≥0, W⊆Y×{0,1}^b, and suppose an extension-query procedure E(y,p) correctly decides whether p extends to z∈{0,1}^b with W(y,z). In the latter case, by induction p had a witness extension and no witness extends p0, so some witness extends p1. Thus the invariant that p has a witness extension is preserved. At length b, p itself is a witness. The query count is b and the total cost is O(b+Σq_i). Lemma (explicit-verifier prefix search). Let Y be finite, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Suppose a deterministic verifier V(y,z) decides membership in W in at most v steps. Given y for which some z satisfies W(y,z), the greedy prefix selector returns such a z using at most b extension checks. Implement each check for a prefix p by enumerating all suffixes u and testing V(y,p||u). The total number of verifier calls is at most 2^b-1, so the running time is O((2^b-1)(v+b)+b^2), including string handling. Proof: Initially the empty prefix has a witness. At prefix p of length i, test whether p||0 has a witness by enumerating its 2^(b-i-1) completions and applying V. If one succeeds, append 0; otherwise the maintained witness extending p must extend p||1, so append 1. Thus after b steps the resulting full string is in W. There are b checks, and their enumeration sizes sum to sum_{i=0}^{b-1} 2^(b-i-1)=2^b-1. The stated bound follows by charging at most v+b per verifier call and O(b^2) for prefix bookkeeping. Scope: this is an explicit upper bound for directly verifiable witness relations; it is exponential in b and does not establish the QE* resource bounds or close OBL-QE-W.

statement: Restricted witness-selector lemma. Let y be an input and suppose its witnesses are exactly the solutions z∈F₂^b of a given linear system A_y z=c_y. For any prefix p, extendibility is decidable by substituting p into the system and testing consistency by Gaussian elimination. Starting with the empty prefix, query extendibility after appending 0; choose 0 if consistent, and otherwise choose 1. Since the current prefix has a solution extension, one of these choices remains consistent. After b choices the resulting string is a witness. The selector uses at most b consistency tests and polynomial time in the input system size.
evidence: Direct invariant proof: before each choice the current prefix has a solution extension; the two possible next bits partition those extensions, so at least one branch remains consistent. Gaussian elimination decides each branch in polynomial time. This is a restricted subclass only; no link to SearchMCSP witnesses or closure of G0001 has been established.

statement: Black-box prefix-query lower bound. For every b>=0, consider hidden z in {0,1}^b and the oracle E_z(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of z. Any deterministic algorithm that identifies z for every hidden z requires at least b oracle queries in the worst case. Proof: each query returns one bit, so a decision tree of depth q has at most 2^q leaves. Correct identification of all 2^b possible hidden strings requires at least 2^b distinct leaves; hence 2^q >= 2^b and q >= b. The bound is attained by querying the successive prefixes along the hidden string, as in prefix self-reduction. Scope: black-box query complexity only; it gives no lower bound on the cost of computing a QE* extension predicate.
proof: Fix b and suppose a deterministic algorithm identifies every hidden z using at most q queries. Its interaction tree has branching factor at most two and depth at most q, hence at most 2^q leaves. Two different hidden strings cannot reach the same leaf, because the algorithm would then output the same string on both and be wrong on at least one. Therefore the tree has at least 2^b leaves, so q>=b. Querying prefixes incrementally identifies z in b queries, proving tightness.

statement: Layered-DAG witness search. Let G=(V,E) be an explicitly supplied directed acyclic graph with layers V_0,...,V_b, edges only from V_i to V_{i+1}, source s in V_0, and accepting set A subseteq V_b. Backward marking decides whether s reaches A in O(|V|+|E|) time; if so, following marked successors outputs a path in O(b) additional time. Proof: mark A; for i=b-1 down to 0 mark v in V_i iff it has an edge to a marked vertex in V_{i+1}. By backward induction a vertex is marked exactly when it has a path to A. Hence s is marked iff a witness path exists. At each marked vertex before V_b choose a marked successor, which yields an accepting path. Each vertex and edge is scanned at most constantly many times. Scope: explicit layered-DAG representation only; no such representation is established for the QE* witness relation.

evidence: A direct induction on prefix length proves correctness, including the b=0 boundary; the running time sums the per-depth exact query costs. This is conditional on efficient E and does not establish those costs for QE*.
proved_step: statement: Depth-sensitive prefix selector lemma. Let Y be a finite set, b≥0, and W⊆Y×{0,1}^b. For each y and prefix p of length i≤b, define E(y,p)=1 iff some z∈{0,1}^b extending p satisfies (y,z)∈W. Suppose an exact deterministic procedure answers every E(y,p) query at depth i in time at most q_i. Then for every y having a W-witness, a deterministic algorithm outputs such a witness in at most b queries and time at most Σ_{i=0}^{b-1}q_i+O(b), plus output handling. Proof: initialize p=ε; by hypothesis E(y,ε)=1. At depth i<b query E(y,p0). If it is 1, replace p by p0. Otherwise replace p by p1. The invariant E(y,p)=1 is preserved: in the second case some witness extends p, and none extends p0, so every witness extending p must extend p1. After b iterations p has length b and E(y,p)=1, which by definition means (y,p)∈W. The time bound is the sum of the b query bounds and O(1) per query/update. If b=0, the premise E(y,ε)=1 directly gives (y,ε)∈W and the empty sum applies.

statement: Exhaustive suffix implementation of prefix extension. Let Y be finite, b≥0, W⊆Y×{0,1}^b, and let V(y,z) decide membership in W in time at most v for every y,z. At a prefix p of length i<b, E(y,p) can be computed by enumerating all 2^(b−i) suffixes and applying V, in time at most 2^(b−i)v plus enumeration overhead. Consequently, the prefix selector that tests E(y,p0) at depths i=0,…,b−1 finds a witness whenever one exists, using at most (2^b−1)v verifier time plus enumeration and selector overhead. Proof: For each tested p0 at depth i, exactly 2^(b−i−1) strings extend p0, so the verifier work summed over depths is v·Σ_{i=0}^{b−1}2^(b−i−1)=v(2^b−1). Each query is exact by exhaustive enumeration. The selector preserves the invariant that its current prefix has a W-witness extension: if p0 has one, append 0; otherwise, since p has one, a witness extends p1. After b choices the full string is a witness. For b=0, no suffix queries are needed and the initial empty prefix is already a witness under the premise. Scope: this is conditional on the stated verifier and gives an exponential exhaustive implementation; it establishes no useful QE* resource bound and closes no QE* reduction obligation.

evidence: Constructive direct-list algorithm and induction proof; a finite verification was requested independently on all nonempty witness relations through b=4. This bound depends on the explicit witness-list size L and therefore does not establish the required QE* resource bound.
proved_step: statement: Explicit-witness-list selector bound. Let b be a nonnegative integer and let W be a nonempty explicitly listed subset of {0,1}^b, with L=|W|. A deterministic algorithm returns a member of W using at most b prefix-extension queries, each answered by scanning the list, in O(b^2 L) bit comparisons and O(b) extension queries. Proof: initialize the empty prefix p. For each i=0,...,b-1, scan W to determine whether some w in W has prefix p0. If so set p:=p0; otherwise set p:=p1. Inductively p is a prefix of some member of W: this holds initially; if the scan finds an extension by 0 it remains true, and if not, the maintained witness must extend by 1. After b iterations p is a length-b member of W. Each iteration compares at most L strings against a prefix of length at most b, costing O(bL), hence the total O(b^2L). The algorithm is correct for all nonempty W, including b=0, where W={empty string} and no scans are needed.

evidence: Complete induction proof is included in the statement. This is a constructive selector using exact prefix counts rather than explicit witness-list scans or Boolean extension queries; it isolates exact counting as a sufficient implementation target, without asserting that QE* admits an efficient counter.
proved_step: statement: Prefix-count selector lemma. Let Y be finite, b≥0, and W⊆Y×{0,1}^b. Define the prefix-count oracle C(y,p)=|{z∈{0,1}^b : W(y,z) and p is a prefix of z}|. For any y with C(y,ε)>0, a deterministic algorithm finds z with W(y,z) using at most b oracle queries: at each step, query C(y,p0), append 0 if the answer is positive, and otherwise append 1. Proof: maintain C(y,p)>0, true initially by hypothesis. If C(y,p0)>0, the invariant holds after appending 0. Otherwise, since every extension of p begins with either 0 or 1 and C(y,p)>0, C(y,p1)=C(y,p)>0, so it holds after appending 1. After b steps p has length b; its only length-b extension is itself, hence C(y,p)>0 implies W(y,p). This includes b=0, where the initial positive count already certifies the empty string. The lemma reduces witness selection to exact prefix counting; it gives no resource bound for implementing that counting oracle for QE* witnesses.

statement: Prefix-extension selector interface lemma. Let b be a nonnegative integer, Y any set, W a subset of Y × {0,1}^b, and E(y,p)=1 exactly when there exists z∈{0,1}^b extending p with (y,z)∈W. For each fixed y with a W-witness, the following deterministic procedure outputs z with (y,z)∈W using at most b calls to E and O(b) additional bit operations: start with p=ε; for i=1,…,b query E(y,p0); if the answer is 1 set p←p0, otherwise set p←p1; output p. Proof: inductively, before iteration i, p is a length-(i−1) prefix having at least one W-extension. Initially this holds by the assumed witness. If E(y,p0)=1 then p0 has an extension; if it is 0, the maintained existence of an extension of p implies that every such extension begins with 1, so p1 has an extension. Thus the invariant holds after each iteration. At i=b, the length-b string p is its own only extension, hence (y,p)∈W. There is one E query per bit and only linear work to append/read bits. Scope: exact deterministic search conditional on an exact extension predicate; it does not bound E's computation time/space or prove that QE* supplies E within its resource limits.

statement: Fixed-fiber advice-pattern capacity. Let F be any finite set, s>=0, and D:{0,1}^s x F->{0,1}. Define P_a:F->{0,1} by P_a(x)=D(a,x). Then |{P_a:a in {0,1}^s}|<=2^s. Proof: the map a |-> P_a has domain {0,1}^s, which has cardinality 2^s; its image therefore has cardinality at most 2^s. In particular, any labeling of F outside this family cannot be represented by this fixed decoder with s advice bits. Scope: a capacity bound for decoders whose varying input across F is only a; it does not imply label constancy, efficient advice construction, or a QE* reduction.

statement: Constructive missing-label consequence of fixed-decoder capacity. Let F be a finite set with |F|=f, s>=0, and D:{0,1}^s x F->{0,1} be fixed. If s<f, there exists a labeling L:F->{0,1} that no advice string realizes, and it can be found by enumerating the 2^f labelings and rejecting those among P_a(x)=D(a,x), in at most 2^f * 2^s * f bit evaluations plus lexicographic bookkeeping. Proof: the image family P={P_a} has size at most 2^s, while the set of all labelings has size 2^f. Since s<f, 2^s<2^f, so P is a proper subset. Enumerate labelings in lexicographic order, compare each to all P_a, and return the first absent pattern; at least one exists by the strict cardinality inequality. This is a constructive finite decoder lower bound only. It does not apply to OBL-QE-W's decoder D(x,W), where x is an additional varying input, and closes no QE* obligation.

statement: Deterministic bounded-witness selector lemma. Let X,Y be finite sets, R:X→Y, and L:X→{0,1}. Suppose each relevant T has at least one witness w of length at most b(T), and a deterministic verifier V(T,w) accepts exactly the admissible witnesses in time at most v(T). Suppose D(x,w) runs in time at most d(x) and equals L(x) for every x and every admissible witness of R(x). Then L is decidable by enumerating all strings w of length at most b(R(x)), returning the first accepted witness, and applying D. The running time is at most (2^{b+1}-1)v(R(x))+d(x)+time(R), where b=max_T b(T) over the relevant outputs. In particular, this gives a polynomial-time decision procedure when these quantities and 2^b are polynomially bounded. Proof: for T=R(x), the enumeration includes an admissible witness by hypothesis; exactness of V ensures the selected string is admissible. The universal correctness assumption on D then gives D(x,w)=L(x). The time bound counts every tested string and the final decoder call. This lemma requires deterministic verification within the stated bound; witness length alone does not imply efficient selection.
proof: As stated in the step: exhaustive enumeration covers all strings of length at most b, exact verification returns an admissible witness because one exists, and universal decoder correctness gives the answer. Summing the verifier costs and decoder/reduction costs yields the bound.

statement: Tight black-box query bound for prefix-extension search. For each integer b >= 0, let the hidden witness be z in {0,1}^b and give a deterministic algorithm oracle access only to E_z(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of z, for arbitrary binary strings p (including the empty string). If the algorithm must output z correctly for every hidden z, then its worst-case number of oracle queries is at least b. The bound is attained by querying the b prefixes 0, 1, ..., z_{<b}0 successively as in the standard bit-by-bit selector (for b=0, output the empty string with zero queries). Proof: The oracle E_z is exactly membership in the set of prefixes of z. Any deterministic algorithm making at most q yes/no queries has at most 2^q possible answer transcripts and hence at most 2^q possible outputs as functions of the transcript. Correctness for all 2^b possible z requires at least 2^b distinct output transcripts, so 2^q >= 2^b and q >= b. Conversely, after a known prefix p of z, query E_z(p0); append 0 on yes and 1 on no. This identifies each next bit in one query, yielding z in b queries. Scope: black-box query complexity only; the oracle may be computationally expensive, so this gives no QE* resource bound and does not show the extension predicate itself is hard.

statement: For any explicitly known nonempty finite set W⊆{0,1}^b fixed in advance, a selector can return a member of W with zero oracle queries.
proof: Choose w0∈W before receiving the input and output w0. Since w0∈W, the output is a valid witness, and no query is used. Thus query lower bounds require an access model where the input-dependent witness set is not explicitly known.
scope: Fixed, explicitly known W only; this does not construct a selector for an input-dependent hidden witness set.
diagnostic: This is a query-model clarification, not P≠NP progress. It makes no barrier-circumvention claim.

statement: Hidden-singleton prefix-query complexity. For every integer b>=1, let an unknown witness w range over {0,1}^b, and let the only allowed query be E(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of w, for any binary string p of length at most b. Any deterministic adaptive algorithm that identifies w for every possible w requires at least b queries in the worst case; querying the prefixes of lengths 1,...,b achieves b queries.
proof: For the lower bound, consider the binary decision tree of a deterministic algorithm. Each query has two possible answers, so a depth-d tree has at most 2^d leaves. Correct identification of each of the 2^b possible witnesses requires at least 2^b distinct leaves, hence d>=b. For the upper bound, query the length-i prefix of the bits already recovered followed by 0, for i=1,...,b. A yes answer sets bit i to 0; a no answer sets it to 1, since the hidden witness is known to exist and its preceding bits have already been recovered. After b queries all bits are determined.
scope: Exact deterministic worst-case query complexity in the hidden-singleton prefix-membership oracle model. It does not establish that a QE* witness relation is hidden, singleton-valued, or inaccessible by other computations, so it does not close the QE* obligation.
diagnostic: The oracle property is relativizing and localizing; the argument is combinatorial and does not yield a natural property or algebraic circuit lower bound. No P!=NP progress is claimed.

statement: Depth-sensitive prefix-extension selector. Let Y be finite, b>=0, W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Suppose for every relevant y and every prefix p of length i<b, E(y,p)=1 iff p extends to z with W(y,z) can be computed in time at most q_i. Given y with a W-witness, a deterministic algorithm finds one using at most b extension queries and time O(b + sum_{i=0}^{b-1} q_i). Proof: begin with empty prefix p, which has a witness extension by assumption. At depth i, query E(y,p0). If true, replace p by p0; otherwise replace p by p1. In the latter case the invariant supplies an extension of p and the failed query rules out p0, so p1 has an extension. Thus after each query the invariant holds. At depth b, p is a full-length string with W(y,p), and the sum of query costs plus O(b) bookkeeping gives the stated bound. Scope: conditional selector bound only; it does not prove the QE* extension predicate has these costs.
proof: The invariant is that the current prefix p has some extension z with W(y,z). Initially this follows from the assumed existence of a witness. If E(y,p0)=1, choose p0 and preserve the invariant. If E(y,p0)=0, an extension of p exists by the invariant, and none extends p0; since the next bit is binary, an extension must extend p1. After b iterations the prefix has length b, so its only extension is itself and it satisfies W. There is one query at each depth i, costing at most q_i, plus O(b) prefix-management time.

statement: Verifier-to-extension bound for fixed-length witnesses. Let Y be a finite input set, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Suppose a deterministic verifier V(y,z) decides membership in W and runs in at most T(y,b) time on every z of length b. For each prefix p of length i<=b define E(y,p)=1 iff some z in {0,1}^b extending p satisfies V(y,z)=1. Then E is computable in at most 2^(b-i) (T(y,b)+O(b)) time, up to polynomial overhead for enumerating and supplying suffixes. Consequently, on any y having a W-witness, the binary prefix selector finds one in at most b queries and total time O(b + sum_{i=0}^{b-1} 2^(b-i-1)(T(y,b)+b)); in particular this is O(2^b(T(y,b)+b)). If b <= c log_2 s and T(y,b) <= s^d for fixed constants c,d, the selector runs in polynomial time in s. Proof: for fixed (y,p), enumerate all 2^(b-i) suffixes u of length b-i and run V(y,pu); return 1 upon the first acceptance and 0 if all reject. This is exactly E by its definition and uses at most 2^(b-i) verifier calls, each costing T(y,b), plus O(b) per candidate to form or manage the string, yielding the stated bound. Apply the prefix-selector invariant: initially the empty prefix has a witness; at depth i query E(y,p0), retain p0 if true, otherwise retain p1, which must have an extension because p has one and p0 has none. After b stages the prefix is itself a verified witness. Summing the query bounds gives O(b + (T+b) sum_{i=0}^{b-1}2^(b-i-1)) = O(b+ (T+b)(2^b-1)) = O(2^b(T+b)). Finally, if b<=c log_2 s, then 2^b<=s^c, so the bound is polynomial in s. Scope: this supplies a sufficient condition for a polynomial-time witness selector, conditional on a polynomial-time verifier and logarithmic witness length; it does not establish that QE* has logarithmic-length witnesses or a QE*-specific verifier bound.
